To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pericentric inversion rate is much lower compared to the paracentric one, that paracentric inversion tract length is approx 4.8Mb, and that the number of short inversions is much larger than the number of long inversions.

pericentric inversion rates are much lower than paracentric inversion rates, and that there is a correlation between the position of the two breakpoints defining an inversion such that short tract lengths are favored.
pericentric and short paracentric invasions occur at a much smaller rate than paracentric inversion and that there is a bias towards short inversion tract lengths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of the distribution and rate of paracentric invversions in Drosophila.
the evolution of inversions.
the estimation of the rate of pericentric versus paracentric inversion and the distribution of tract lengths of paracentric inversons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the distribution of inversion lengths has an even greater prepondance of shorter inversions than would be predicted if the breakpoints were uniformly and independently distributed.

the distribution of tract lengths in the Drosophila genome is non-random, and the most parsimonious explanation of this is that the rate of paracentric inversion is inversely proportional to tract length.
there is a strong correlation between the length of a tract and the chance of acceptance, but that there is a significant bias in favor of short tract lengths.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of paracentric inversion is proportional to the tract length, and the rate is higher for short inversions compared to longer ones.
the method developed in this article provides the first statistical method for estimating the distribution for inversion tract lengths from molecular marker data.
the rate of paracentric inversion is proportional to tract length and the rate of pericentric inversion is proportional but with a smaller coefficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of tract lengths is not uniform.
the rate of paracentric inversion is strongly dependent on tract length.
the relative rates of inversions of different lengths are not uniform.
